# Admin OpenAPI sketch stays one generated file; source splits by domain

`docs/contracts/admin.openapi.yaml` is emitted verbatim from `emitAdminOpenApiDocument()` (`packages/contract/src/admin/openapi.ts`) via `pnpm --filter @webhook-broadcast/contract run emit:openapi`, and `check:openapi` fails CI if the committed file and the Zod emission diverge (`packages/contract/scripts/check-admin-openapi-drift.ts`). At ~1670 lines it crosses the general 1k-line maintainability smell, but it is a **generated artifact**, not hand-authored prose: nobody edits it directly (a drift-checked `pnpm contract:emit` round-trip would just overwrite manual edits), nobody diffs it path-by-path in review (the diff that matters is the Zod source diff), and splitting it into tagged partials (`channels.yaml`, `broadcasts.yaml`, …) would require `$ref`-stitching or a bundler step in both `emit:openapi` and `generate:client` for no reviewer benefit — openapi-typescript and the drift check both need one resolved document anyway. So we take option 2 from issue #30: treat the emitted YAML as the sole committed artifact layout, and put the reviewable module boundary where humans actually read and edit this contract — the Zod source.

`adminOpenApiPaths` (the thing that used to be one 370-line object) is now composed from seven per-domain modules under `packages/contract/src/admin/paths/`: `channels.ts`, `channelFailures.ts`, `endpoints.ts`, `tokens.ts`, `operatorTokens.ts`, `broadcasts.ts`, `deliveries.ts`, each named for the OpenAPI `tag` it declares and each under 100 lines, plus a `shared.ts` holding only what more than one of them actually uses: the common `default` error response, the operator security requirement, and the `{channelId}` path-param schema every channel-scoped domain hangs off. A path-param schema used by a single domain (`{deliveryId}`, `{tokenId}`, `{channelId}/{endpointId}`, …) is declared in that domain's own module, so the shared surface stays small and a domain module reads top-to-bottom without a detour. Each module closes with `satisfies ZodOpenApiPathsObject`, so a malformed operation is reported in the module that owns it rather than at the spread site. `openapi.ts` itself is now just the `createDocument(...)` call and an object spread of those seven modules — the file a reviewer actually opens to understand or extend an admin route stays small and stays split by domain; only the build output that downstream tooling (openapi-typescript, the drift check) consumes as a single document stays a single file.

This is the general rule going forward for this contract: if a future domain's Zod-declared paths module grows past ~1k lines on its own, split *that* module — the sketch YAML is exempt from the smell because it is derived, not authored.
